doc.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Why Black musicians became great soloists
summary: With staff bands and symphonies closed to them, Black musicians learned to play solos to get nightclub work.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Symphony orchestra, you could look forward to doing that, but what was the use of studying diligently and then you’d be refused? So, first thing you’d learn how to do was play a solo so you could go to a nightclub or one of these joints and get you a gig, working a night club. So, I think that’s why black musicians become great soloists because they concentrated on playing solos.
